;Armed conflicts and attacks
*[[Camp Simba attack]]
**An attack by [[Al-Shabaab (militant group)|Al-Shabaab]] militants on an airfield used by [[Kenya Army|Kenyan]] and [[U.S. troops]] in [[Lamu County]], [[Kenya]], is repelled, leaving four militants dead and five arrested. [https://www.foxnews.com/world/kenya-military-base-used-by-us-kenyan-troops-attacked-by-al-shabab-4-attackers-reported-killed (Fox News)]
**Three [[Americans]] are confirmed to have been killed in the attack, a [[United States Armed Forces|serviceman]] and two [[Private military company|contractors]]. [https://www.cnn.com/2020/01/05/politics/us-service-member-civilian-defense-contractors-killed-kenya/index.html (CNN)] [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-africa-50997769 (BBC News)]
*In [[Metz]], [[Grand Est]], [[France]], an assailant shouting [[Takbir|"Allahu Akbar"]] attempts to stab [[Law enforcement in France|police officers]] with a knife before being shot and injured. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-france-security/french-police-shoot-and-wound-knifeman-shouting-allahu-akbar-in-metz-idUSKBN1Z40ON (Reuters)]
*[[American-led intervention in Iraq (2014–2021)]]
**[[United States Central Command]] releases a [[Combined Joint Task Force – Operation Inherent Resolve|CJTF-OIR]] statement announcing that it "has paused" operations against [[Islamic State of Iraq and the Levant |ISIL]] in order to concentrate on protecting their troops at bases in Iraq. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2020/jan/05/anti-isis-coalition-suspends-operations-as-iraqi-mps-vote-to-expel-us-troops (''The Guardian'')]

;Disasters and accidents
*[[2019–20 Australian bushfire season]]
**A bushfire leads to the residents of [[Eden, New South Wales]], to [[emergency evacuation|evacuate]]. [https://www.abc.net.au/news/2020-01-05/fires-nsw-eden-evacuation-ordered-as-blaze-poses-imminent-risk/11841864 (ABC News and Current Affairs)]
*In the early hours of the morning, a car crashes into a group of [[Germany|German]] tourists in [[Luttach]], [[Italy]], killing six people and injuring 11 others. The driver was reportedly drunk and is charged with murder. [https://www.bangkokpost.com/world/1829234/six-germans-die-as-drunk-driver-hits-pedestrians-in-italian-alps (''Bangkok Post'')]
*Thirty-six people are killed and others injured after a building under construction [[structural integrity and failure|collapses]] in [[Kep Province|Kep]], [[Cambodia]]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-cambodia-collapse/cambodia-building-collapse-kills-36-people-injures-23-others-idUSKBN1Z401D (Reuters)]
*A vehicle pile-up involving multiple [[semi-truck]]s and a [[tour bus]] on the [[Pennsylvania Turnpike]] in [[Westmoreland County, Pennsylvania]], [[U.S.]] leaves five dead and 60 injured. [https://www.foxnews.com/us/pennsylvania-turnpike-crash-multiple-dead-tour-bus-semi-trucks (Fox News)]

;Law and crime
*[[Japan]] says it will tighten [[immigration to Japan|immigration]] measures after the escape of former Chairman of [[Nissan]] [[Carlos Ghosn]] from the country. The [[Japanese government]] condemns Ghosn's escape as "unjustifiable". [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-nissan-ghosn/japan-orders-tighter-immigration-procedures-after-ghosn-flees-country-idUSKBN1Z402U (Reuters)] [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2020/01/japan-condemns-unjustifiable-escape-carlos-ghosn-200105042549506.html (Al Jazeera)]
*[[2019–20 Hong Kong protests]]
**Thousands of protesters march in the [[Sheung Shui]] neighborhood; dozens are arrested. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-hongkong-protests/dozens-arrested-after-hong-kong-protest-taking-aim-at-chinese-traders-idUSKBN1Z405K (Reuters)]

;Politics and elections
*[[2020 Venezuelan National Assembly Delegated Committee election]]
**Elected deputies in Venezuela vote for a President of the [[National Assembly (Venezuela)|National Assembly]], who [[Venezuelan presidential crisis|may be able to claim]] the nation's Presidency. [https://www.miamiherald.com/news/nation-world/world/americas/venezuela/article238905873.html (''Miami Herald'')]
**Despite trying to enter and vote, self-declared interim [[President of Venezuela|president]] [[Juan Guaidó]] is denied entry to the Assembly. Dissident opposition politician [[Luis Parra]] is sworn in as National Assembly president after an impromptu vote. Opposition supporters call it a "parliamentary coup"; the United States denounce a "farce". State broadcasters label Parra as the new speaker of parliament. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-latin-america-51000419 (BBC News)] [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-venezuela-politics/venezuelas-guaido-loses-control-of-congress-opposition-denounces-coup-idUSKBN1Z40J4 (Reuters)]
*In a session boycotted by most [[Iraqis#Religion|Sunni Arab]] and [[Kurds|Kurdish]] representatives, the [[Council of Representatives of Iraq]] accepts a resolution to expel [[United States Army|U.S. troops]] from [[Iraq]]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-iraq-security/iraq-calls-for-foreign-forces-to-leave-after-u-s-killing-of-iran-commander-idUSKBN1Z409A (Reuters)]
*[[U.S. President]] [[Donald Trump]] threatens Iraq—if the U.S. would be required to leave the country—with a bill for a "very extraordinarily expensive" air base and also with sanctions that would "make [[United States sanctions against Iran|Iranian sanctions]] look somewhat tame". [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-iraq-security/iraq-wants-foreign-troops-out-after-air-strike-trump-threatens-sanctions-idUSKBN1Z409A (Reuters)]
*After the [[United States]] kills Iranian General [[Qasem Soleimani]] in the [[2020 Baghdad International Airport airstrike]], [[Islamic Consultative Assembly|Iran's parliament]] votes to exit the 2015 [[Joint Comprehensive Plan of Action]] nuclear deal with world powers. This comes after the United States [[United States withdrawal from the Joint Comprehensive Plan of Action|unilaterally withdrew]] in 2018. [https://www.msn.com/en-us/news/world/iran-abandons-nuclear-deal-over-us-killing-general/ar-BBYDgL8 (MSN)]
*[[2019–20 Croatian presidential election]] 
**The [[runoff election]] for the [[President of Croatia|Croatian Presidency]] is held today, with incumbent [[Kolinda Grabar-Kitarović]] facing former [[Prime Minister of Croatia|Prime Minister]] [[Zoran Milanović]]. [https://www.euronews.com/2020/01/04/croatia-presidential-election-voters-choose-head-of-state-days-after-starting-six-month-eu (Euronews)]
**Milanović is elected.  Grabar-Kitarović pledges a "civilised transfer" of power. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2020/jan/06/croatia-elects-leftist-zoran-milanovic-to-be-next-president (''The Guardian'')]
*[[2019–20 Uzbek parliamentary election]]
**A repeat vote is held in 25 electoral districts in the second round of the latest parliamentary election in [[Uzbekistan]]. [https://tass.com/world/1105859 (TASS)]
*[[Politics of Israel]]
**[[Prime Minister of Israel]] [[Benjamin Netanyahu]] announces appointments at several ministries he had to drop following his [[Investigations involving Benjamin Netanyahu|indictment for corruption]]. [[David Bitan]], who is under suspicion of accepting bribes, is appointed as [[Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Development (Israel)|Minister of Agriculture]]. [https://www.ynetnews.com/article/S1ZgqYygU (Ynet)]
*People in [[Pakistan]] protest in [[Karachi]] over the [[2020 Baghdad International Airport airstrike|U.S. killing]] of [[Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps]] general [[Qasem Soleimani]]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-pakistan-protests-iran-idUSKBN1Z40NR (Reuters)]
